name: RecallWhy
tagline: Agents that tell a retailer which recalled products are on its shelves — and why they believe it.

entry_points.api: npm run api  →  POST /run {since, only?, limit?}
entry_points.docker: docker build -t recallwhy . && docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 recallwhy

agents.name: Cartographer
agents.role: Before any case, maps the fragmented sources through Zetaris: lists datasources, Lightning databases and views, tags barcode/SKU/lot columns, profiles barcode lengths and tests cross-source barcode joins as written and normalised (finds GTIN-14 padding from a third of suppliers). The Auditor uses the join it verified and sends back rows it cannot reach; the Cartographer then diagnoses that supplier, tests the fix on all of its ship notices and corrects the map.

agents.name: Scout
agents.role: Reads live CPSC and FDA recall feeds and the item master through Zetaris; one federated REST x JDBC UPC sweep; opens one case per recall that touches the catalog.

agents.name: Investigator
agents.role: Decides which candidate SKUs a recall covers (UPC/model rules, NVIDIA Nemotron judge for text matches, H-MEM prior decisions), reads lot codes, computes exposure with federated SQL.

agents.name: Auditor
agents.role: Can block. Re-checks UPCs against the live notice in Zetaris, checks quotes and lot codes are verbatim in the notice, re-derives every exposure number with its own SQL, rejects briefs that state unsupported numbers. Max 2 revision rounds, then escalates to a human queue.

agents.name: Briefer
agents.role: Writes the action brief only from the World Model context builder, citing evidence ids.

zetaris.how: All agent data access is Zetaris Lightning SQL over its REST API. Two live Lightning REST tables (saferproducts.gov CPSC recalls, a top-level JSON array; api.fda.gov food enforcement) flattened into schemastore views, and two JDBC datasources (synthetic ERP and supplier-portal Postgres databases). Agents run federated queries joining live REST feeds with JDBC tables and the two databases with each other; the Auditor re-queries Zetaris independently to verify numbers. The Cartographer agent maps the sources through Zetaris's catalog statements (SHOW DATASOURCES, SHOW DATASOURCE TABLES, DESCRIBE DATASOURCE TABLE, SHOW LIGHTNING DATABASES, SHOW TABLES IN, DESCRIBE) and tests cross-source barcode joins with federated SQL; it finds that a third of the suppliers send GTIN-14 barcodes (7,856 of 14,180 ship notices join as written, 12,785 without leading zeros) and leaves the other 1,395 open. When the Auditor sends back ship-notice rows its key cannot reach, the Cartographer diagnoses that supplier's barcodes with federated SQL, tests the transform on every ship notice from the supplier, and corrects the map (e.g. suppliers that drop the UPC check digit).

meterless.how: Two Meterless agent engines mounted from github.com/Meterless/Meterless (Apache-2.0 reference implementations): H-MEM stores every adjudication (agent, medium trust) and every human decision (high trust) and is read before each judgement; World Model holds source maps, recall, case and finding facts with provenance (which SQL, which agent, which model call), and its context builder is the only input the Briefer sees. Tests: test/engines.test.ts (a human decision from session 1 changes the session-2 decision after a restart; World Model ids converge across agents and facts keep their query ids). Meterless Nightshift is the primary AI provider: every model call goes to its OpenAI-compatible Runtime API (127.0.0.1:8088/v1, meterless-app/meterless-scope headers), and the trace records the receipt id and routed model of each call.

cursor.how: Repository developed in Cursor. The Cursor agent (CLI, Auto model) scaffolded the project, wrote the synthetic retailer generator and Postgres loader, the Zetaris REST runner and the DuckDB sample-mode runner with their tests; each change was reviewed and fixed before committing (see commit messages marked 'Cursor agent').

nvidia.how: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B, called through Meterless Nightshift (the NVIDIA key is in Nightshift's provider store), is the default model behind the single injected generator: it judges text matches between a recall notice and an item-master line (and must quote the notice), reads lot codes out of messy code_info text, and writes the why-paragraph that the Auditor checks. Each call's routed model is recorded in the trace and shown in the viewer and report.
nvidia.evaluation: eval/EVAL.md: Nemotron 3 Ultra through Nightshift catches 186/194 covered pairs over 440 (rules alone: 103), 4 wrongly dismissed, 6 false alarms, 23 to a human, 0 of 537 model calls failed; on text matches the Auditor cuts the judge's first-answer dismissals 12 → 4 and false alarms 9 → 6

live: CPSC SaferProducts Recall API (U.S. government, public domain)
openFDA food enforcement API (public domain, CC0 per open.fda.gov/license)
data.synthetic: Northwind Mercantile retailer: stores, item master, inventory lots, weekly sales, supplier ship notices — generated by scripts/gen-synthetic.ts (seeded). About 120 SKUs are deliberately derived from real recall notices so the catalog overlaps the feeds; ground truth for evaluation is kept in data/synthetic/eval/ and never read by the agents. No personal data.
data.sample_snapshots: sample/ holds feed snapshots captured on the date in sample/CAPTURED_AT for SAMPLE_MODE.

pre_existing_work: Matching ideas (brand gate, product-kind overlap, model-number conflicts, grounded quotes) were adapted from the author's Recall Sloth project (github.com/mikey92/recall-sloth, committed 21 Oct 2026). Code in this repository was written during the build window. Third-party code: src/engines/hmem and src/engines/world-model are the Meterless reference implementations (Apache-2.0), mounted with the changes listed in each CHANGES.md.
sample_mode: SAMPLE_MODE=true (or no Zetaris credentials) runs the same agents and SQL against an in-process DuckDB stand-in over the sample snapshots and synthetic CSVs; output is labelled SAMPLE and Zetaris is not used.
